fieldData.name: AI Citations: How to Get Cited by AI Search
fieldData.meta-title: How to Get Cited by AI Search: The Complete Guide
fieldData.meta-description: How to get cited by AI search across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overviews: the four shared requirements, what differs per platform, and how to measure it.
fieldData.post-summary: The hub guide to AI citations: the four requirements every platform shares, a platform by platform breakdown of where ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overviews diverge, why off-domain mentions outweigh on-page work, the structural changes that make pages quotable, how to audit crawler access, and how to measure citations without reading variance as progress.
fieldData.post-body:
To learn how to get cited by AI search, treat it as four requirements rather than a tactic: the system must be able to reach your page, it must find a self-contained claim worth lifting, that claim must be corroborated somewhere it already trusts, and your entity has to be unambiguous enough to name. Every platform weights these differently. None of them skips any of them.

AI citations are the unit of work here, and the discipline that chases them is usually sold as LLM citation optimization. This page is the hub for that subject. It covers what the platforms share, then routes to the page that handles each one in depth, because the mechanics genuinely diverge once you get past the four shared requirements. If you want the underlying concept rather than the practice, our explanation of what LLMO is sets out the vocabulary this page assumes.

The Short Answer: How to Get Cited by AI Search

Be reachable, be quotable, be corroborated, be identifiable. Reachable means the right crawler is permitted and the page renders without JavaScript. Quotable means a declarative sentence that survives being lifted out of context. Corroborated means the same claim appears on sources the system already trusts. Identifiable means your organisation is described consistently everywhere it appears.

What this is not is a ranking exercise. There is no position to hold and no ladder to climb. You are either named in a synthesised answer or you are not, and the same prompt can produce a different set of names on two consecutive runs. That variance is a property of the systems, not a flaw in your work, and it has a direct consequence for measurement that we come back to at the end.

The commercial reason to care has sharpened. Pew Research Center found that users clicked a link on a results page in 8 percent of visits when an AI summary was present, against 15 percent when it was not, and clicked a source cited inside the summary in just 1 percent of visits. A citation is better read as a brand exposure event than as a traffic channel. If you are budgeting for AI visibility on the expectation of referral sessions, the arithmetic will disappoint you.

What AI Systems Look For, Across Every Platform

Access. A crawler that is blocked, or a page whose content only exists after JavaScript runs, cannot be cited at any price. This is the cheapest failure to fix and the most common one we find.

Extractability. Retrieval lifts sentences, not pages. A paragraph that opens with context and arrives at the answer in its fourth sentence loses to one that answers in the first. Declarative, self-contained sentences with the subject named rather than implied are what survive extraction.

Corroboration. A claim that appears only on your own domain is weaker than the same claim echoed on a review platform, a community thread or an independent roundup. This is the factor most teams underweight, and it is why the mentions section below matters more than the structure section.

Entity clarity. If three pages on your own site describe your company differently, a model has to pick one, and the safe choice is to name a competitor whose description is consistent. Google's guidance on AI features in Search frames the whole problem the same way: there is no AI-specific trick, only unique content, clear structure and sound technical access.

How to Get Cited by AI Search, Platform by Platform

The four requirements are shared. How each platform reaches you, and what it does with what it finds, is not. Each section below is the short version; the linked page is the long one.

PlatformHow it reaches youWhat it weights mostThe deep page
Google AI OverviewsGooglebot, with the existing index behind itEstablished ranking signals plus extractable structureRanking in Google AI Overviews
ChatGPTOAI-SearchBot for search, ChatGPT-User for user-triggered fetchesThird party corroboration and category entity clarityGetting cited by ChatGPT
PerplexityIts own crawler plus live retrieval on nearly every answerFreshness and a dense, citable source listGetting cited by Perplexity
ClaudeClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-UserSource quality and internal consistency of the claimGetting cited by Claude
Google GeminiGoogle infrastructure, overlapping with SearchEntity signals and corroboration across the open webGetting cited by Gemini

Google AI Overviews

AI Overviews citations are the most predictable of the five, because Overviews sit on top of the existing index, which makes it the one surface where traditional SEO work transfers almost directly. If you already rank for the query, you are in the candidate pool. The incremental work is structural rather than promotional. Our guide to ranking in Google AI Overviews covers the specifics.

ChatGPT

To get cited by ChatGPT you lean hardest on off-domain presence, because the model is frequently assembling a recommendation set rather than answering a factual question. OpenAI documents three separate agents: GPTBot for training, OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT search, and ChatGPT-User for user-triggered fetches. The first two are independently controllable in robots.txt. OpenAI states that robots rules may not apply to ChatGPT-User, so no vendor can promise you robots.txt control over it. The detail is in getting cited by ChatGPT.

Perplexity

Perplexity retrieves live on nearly every answer and shows its sources, which makes it the fastest surface to get a read on and the most sensitive to freshness. A page updated this month can displace one from last year on the same claim. See getting cited by Perplexity for B2B.

Claude and Gemini

Anthropic runs three agents with different jobs, and Anthropic's guidance for site owners notes that disabling Claude-SearchBot may reduce your visibility in Claude's search results, which is a trade worth making deliberately rather than by default. Gemini draws on Google infrastructure, so entity consistency across the open web carries more weight than any single page. We cover each in getting cited by Claude and getting cited by Google Gemini.

Mentions: The Factor That Outweighs the Rest

If you can only fix one thing, fix this. A claim made only on your own site is an assertion. The same claim appearing on a review platform, a practitioner thread and an independent roundup is a fact as far as a retrieval system is concerned, and the model will reach for the corroborated version.

The practical consequence is that the highest-leverage AI visibility work often happens on pages you do not own: keeping review profiles current and complete, being accurately represented in the category roundups that already rank, and participating genuinely where your buyers ask each other for recommendations. We set out the full argument, and why this now outranks link building, in brand mentions versus backlinks in AI search.

One warning, because the failure mode is expensive. Corroboration that is manufactured reads as manufactured. Seeded threads, sockpuppet accounts and reviews traded for incentives are detectable by the communities they target long before they are detectable by a model, and the reputational cost lands on the brand rather than on the agency that ran it.

Structure: Making Your Pages Quotable

Three changes do most of the work. Open every page with a direct answer of 40 to 70 words that could be lifted whole. Put comparisons in real HTML tables, because tables are the single most frequently extracted element on a page. Write declarative sentences that name their subject, so a sentence removed from its paragraph still parses.

Then do the same at the level above the page. Nine pages on one theme with nothing above them leaves a model unable to tell which represents your position, and the safest behaviour is to quote someone else. Deciding which page owns which question is a structural job, and our playbook for optimising content for LLMs covers the page-level mechanics of it.

One thing to stop doing: treating FAQ markup as a visibility feature. Google's FAQ rich result was deprecated and stopped appearing in Search from May 2026. FAQ schema is still worth adding because it labels a question and answer pair unambiguously for a parser, but it no longer buys you anything in the results page, and anyone selling it as a ranking tactic is working from a stale playbook.

Access: Making Sure AI Can Read You

Check three things, in this order. First, your robots.txt, agent by agent rather than in aggregate, because the agents have different jobs and blanket rules usually block something you wanted. Second, whether your key pages render their content in the initial HTML response, which you can test by fetching the page without executing JavaScript and looking for the paragraph you want quoted. Third, your server logs, for whether these agents are arriving at all.

The common own goal is a blanket disallow added during an unrelated scraping scare and never revisited. It is worth deciding each agent separately: permitting search agents while declining training agents is a coherent position, and it is a different decision from blocking everything.

Measuring Whether You Get Cited by AI Search

Build a fixed prompt set of fifteen to thirty questions a buyer would actually ask, run it on a schedule across the platforms you care about, and record whether you were named, which page was cited, and which competitors appeared beside you. Keep the prompt wording frozen between runs, or you are measuring your own edits.

Then do the step that makes the numbers mean anything: establish the noise floor. Run the identical set twice, with nothing changed in between, and record the spread. Treat movements smaller than that spread as nothing. The same prompt genuinely returns different names on consecutive runs, so without a noise floor every report is unfalsifiable. Method is in measuring LLMO and tracking AI visibility and tooling in the LLMO checklist.

Report presence and share rather than a single score. There is no AI rank, and any number presented as one is a vendor's internal composite. Ask what prompt set produced it and how many runs it averages. If neither question has an answer, the number is decoration.

Get Cited by AI Search With DevCommX

Here is what we will not tell you: that we can guarantee a citation, or hand you an AI rank number, or show you a share of voice figure without publishing the prompt set beside it. None of those things exist, and a vendor offering them is selling you a composite they invented. What we will do is run your prompt set twice before changing anything so you know your noise floor, audit crawler access agent by agent, fix the pages whose answer arrives in the fourth sentence, and tell you plainly when the limiting factor is off-domain corroboration we cannot manufacture for you. That last one is often the answer, and it is the least convenient one to sell. If you want the diagnosis before the proposal, start a conversation and use whatever is useful, whoever you end up hiring.

  • OpenAI, Overview of OpenAI crawlers and user agents, source for the GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User split, their independent robots.txt control, and the statement that robots rules may not apply to ChatGPT-User

FAQ

Where should you start if you want to know how to get cited by AI search?

Four things have to be true at once. The platform's crawler must be able to reach the page and read it without running JavaScript. The page must contain a self-contained declarative claim that survives being lifted out of context. That claim should be corroborated on sources the system already trusts, such as review platforms or independent roundups. And your organisation must be described consistently wherever it appears.

Why does AI cite some sites and not others?

Usually because of corroboration and ambiguity rather than content quality. A claim that appears only on your own domain is weaker than the same claim echoed on independent sources, so the corroborated version gets quoted. Ambiguity compounds it: if several of your own pages answer the same question differently, a model cannot tell which is canonical and will often name a competitor whose position is unambiguous.

How do I appear in AI answers?

Start with access, because a blocked crawler or a JavaScript-rendered page makes everything else irrelevant. Then rewrite the opening of your key pages into a direct 40 to 70 word answer, move comparisons into real HTML tables, and work on off-domain corroboration through review profiles and category roundups. Measure with a fixed prompt set rather than spot checks.

Is getting cited by AI the same across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and AI Overviews?

The four underlying requirements are shared, but the mechanics differ enough to matter. Google AI Overviews sits on the existing search index, so traditional ranking work transfers. ChatGPT leans heavily on third party corroboration. Perplexity retrieves live on nearly every answer and is the most sensitive to freshness. Claude and Gemini weight source quality and entity consistency respectively.

Does getting cited by AI bring traffic?

Very little directly. Pew Research Center found users clicked a source cited inside an AI summary in just 1 percent of visits, so a citation is better understood as a brand exposure event than as a traffic channel. Budget for it on that basis, measure it as presence and share of voice, and keep any referral traffic figure as a separate and heavily caveated number.

Can you control whether AI crawlers access your site?

Mostly, but not completely, and the detail matters. OpenAI documents separate agents for training, search and user-triggered fetches, and the first two are independently controllable in robots.txt. OpenAI states that robots rules may not apply to the user-triggered agent, so no vendor can promise you full control. Anthropic similarly notes that blocking its search agent may reduce your visibility in Claude.
